rows.h: Any other criminal conspiracy (b)
rows.p: Imprisonment for 6 months, or fine, or both

rows.h: Waging or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war against Government of India
rows.p: Death, or imprisonment for life and fine

rows.h: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by u/s 147
rows.p: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for 10 years and fine

rows.h: Collecting arms, etc ,with intension of waging war against government of India
rows.p: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for 10 years and fine

rows.h: Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war
rows.p: Imprisonment for 10 years and fine

rows.h: Assaulting President, Governor , etc, with intent to compel or restrain exercise of any lawful power
rows.p: Imprisonment for 7years and fine

rows.h: Waging war against foreign state at peace with government of India
rows.p: Imprisonment for life and fine or imprisonment for 7 years and fine, or fine

rows.h: Depredation on territories of foreign state at peace with government of India
rows.p: Imprisonment for 7 years and fine, and forfeiture of certain property

rows.h: Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 153 and 154
rows.p: Imprisonment for 7 years and fine, and forfeiture of certain property

rows.h: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of state or war to escape
rows.p: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment for 10 years and fine

rows.h: Public servant negligently suffering prisoner to escape
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 3 years and fine

rows.h: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harboring such prisoner.
rows.p: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment for 10 years and fine

rows.h: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty.
rows.p: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment for 10 years and fine

rows.h: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence there of
rows.p: Death, or imprisonment for life or imprisonment for 10 years and fine

rows.h: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 3 years and fine

rows.p: Imprisonment for 7 years and fine

rows.p: Imprisonment for 2 years, or fine, or both

rows.p: Imprisonment for 2 years, or fine, or both

Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman.

rows.p: Imprisonment for 1 year, or fine, or both

rows.h: Promoting enmity between classes in place of worship, etc.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 5 years and fine

rows.h: Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration
rows.p: Imprisonment for 3 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: If committed in a place of public worship, etc.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 5 years and fine

rows.h: Public servant framing incorrect document with intent to cause injury.

rows.h: Personating public servant.

rows.h: Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent.

rows.p: Fine

rows.h: Failure to keep election accounts.

rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 1 months, or fine of 5,000 rupees, or both

rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 6 months, or fine of 10,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Preventing service of summons or other proceeding, or preventing publication thereof.
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 1 months, or fine of 5,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: If summons, etc., required attendance in person, etc., in a Court
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 6 months, or fine of 10,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant.
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 1 months, or fine of 5,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: If the order requires personal attendance, etc., in a Court
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 6 months, or fine of 10,000 rupees, or both

rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 6 months, or fine of 10,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Intentional omission to give notice or information to public servant by person legally bound to give it.
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 1 months, or fine of 5,000 rupees, or both

rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 6 months, or fine of 10,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Knowingly furnishing false information to public servant

rows.h: If the information required respects the commission of an offence, etc.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 2 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant to make it.
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 6 months, or fine of 5,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Refusing to answer public servant authorised to question.
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 6 months, or fine of 5,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Refusing to sign statement made to a public servant when legally required to do so
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 3 months, or fine of 3,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: False statement on oath or affirmation to public servant or person authorized to administer an oath or affirmation.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 3 years and fine

rows.h: False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 1 year, or with fine of 10,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Resistance to taking of property by lawful authority of a public servant.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 6 months, or fine of 10,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Obstructing sale of property offered for sale by authority of public servant.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 1 month, or fine of 5,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Illegal purchase or bid for property offered for sale by authority of public servant.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 1 month, or fine of 200 rupees, or both

rows.h: Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions
rows.p: Imprisonment for 3 months, or fine of 2,500 rupees, or both

rows.h: Omission to assist public servant when bound by law to give assistance.
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 1 month, or fine of 2,500 rupees, or both

rows.h: Willfully neglecting to aid a public servant who demand aid in the execution of process, the prevention of offences, etc.
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 6 months, or fine of 5,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant.
rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 6 months, or fine of 2,500 rupees, or both

rows.h: If such disobedience caused danger to human life, health or safety, or causes or tend to cause a riot or affray.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 1 year, or fine of 5,000 rupees, or both

rows.h: Threat of injury to public servant.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 2 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: Threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 1 year, or fine, or both

rows.h: Giving false evidence
Fabricating false evidence
Punishment for false evidence (1) Intentionally giving or fabricating false evidence in a judicial proceeding
rows.p: Imprisonment for 7 years and 10,000 rupees

rows.h: (2)Giving or fabricating false evidence in any other case
rows.p: Imprisonment for 3 years and 5,000 rupees

rows.p: The same as for the offence

rows.h: Threatening any person to give false evidence.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 7 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: If innocent person is convicted and sentenced in consequence of false evidence with death, or imprisonment for more than 7 years.
rows.p: The same as for the offence

rows.h: Using evidence known to be false.
rows.p: The same as for giving or fabricating false evidence
rows.st: Non-cognizable According as offence of giving such evidence is bailable or non-bailable

rows.h: Knowingly Issuing or signing false certificate.
rows.p: The same as for giving false evidence

rows.h: Using as true a certificate known to be false.
rows.p: The same as for giving false evidence

rows.h: False statement made in any declaration which is by law receivable as evidence.
rows.p: The same as for giving false evidence

rows.h: Using as true such declaration knowing it to be false.
rows.p: The same as for giving false evidence

rows.p: Imprisonment for 3 years and fine

rows.h: If punishable with less than 10 years imprisonment
rows.p: Imprisonment for one- fourth of the longest term provided for the offence, or fine, or both

rows.h: Giving false information respecting an offence committed.

rows.h: Destruction of document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence.

rows.h: False personation for purpose of act or proceeding in suit or prosecution.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 3 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: Fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution.

rows.h: Fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 2 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due.

rows.h: Dishonestly making false claim in Court.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 2 years and fine

rows.h: Fraudulently obtaining decree for sum not due.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 2 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: False charge of offence made with intent to injure.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 5 years, or fine of 2 lakh rupees, or both

rows.h: Criminal proceeding instituted on a false charge of an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or 10 years or upwards.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 10 years and fine

rows.h: Harbouring offender, if the offence is punishable with death.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 5 years and fine

rows.h: If punishable with imprisonment of life or with imprisonment for 10 years.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 3 years and fine

rows.h: If punishable with imprisonment for 1 year and not for 10 years.
rows.p: Imprisonment for one- fourth of the longest term and of the descriptions, provided for the offence, or fine, or both

rows.h: (b) If punishable with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment for 10 years.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 3 years and fine

rows.h: (c) If punishable with imprisonment for less than 10 years
rows.p: Imprisonment for one- fourth of the longest term, provided for the offence, or fine, or both

rows.h: Offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender. (a) If the offence is punishable with death
rows.p: Imprisonment for 7 years and fine

rows.h: (b) If punishable with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment for 10 years.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 3 years and fine

rows.h: (c) If punishable with imprisonment for less than 10 years
rows.p: Imprisonment for one- fourth of the longest term, provided for the offence, or fine, or both

rows.h: Taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 2 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been ordered. (a) If the offence is punishable with death

rows.h: (b) If punishable with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment for 10 years.

rows.h: (c) I f punishable with imprisonment for less than 10 years
rows.p: Imprisonment for one- fourth of the longest term, provided for the offence, or fine, or both

rows.h: (c) If punishable with imprisonment for less than 10 years

rows.p: Simple imprisonment for 2 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: Resistance or obstruction by a person to his lawful apprehension.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 2 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person or rescuing him from lawful custody.
rows.p: Imprisonment for 2 years, or fine, or both

rows.h: If charged with an offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for 10 years

rows.h: If charged with offence punishable with death

rows.h: If the person sentenced to imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for 10 years, or upwards.

rows.h: If under sentence of death
rows.p: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for 10 years and fine

55.h: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
55.t:
55.Whoever abets the commission of an offence punishable
with death or imprisonment for life, shall, if that offence be not
committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express
provision is made under this Sanhita for the punishment of such
abetment, be punished with imprisonment of either description
for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable
to fine; and if any act for which the abettor is liable in consequence
of the abetment, and which causes hurt to any person, is done, the
abettor shall be liable to imprisonment of either description for a
term which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable
to fine.

55.h: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
55.t:
55. Whoever abets the commission of an offence punishable
with death or imprisonment for life, shall, if that offence be not
committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express
provision is made under this Sanhita for the punishment of such
abetment, be punished with imprisonment of either description
for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable
to fine; and if any act for which the abettor is liable in consequence
of the abetment, and which causes hurt to any person, is done, the
abettor shall be liable to imprisonment of either description for a
term which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable
to fine. Illustration. A instigates B to murder Z. The offence is not
committed. If B had murdered Z, he would have been subject to
the punishment of death or imprisonment for life. Therefore, A is
liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years
and also to a fine; and if any hurt be done to Z in consequence of
the abetment, he will be liable to imprisonment for a term which
may extend to fourteen years, and to fine.

57.h: Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons.
57.t:
57. Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public
generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall
be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term
which may extend to seven years and with fine.

58.h: 58 (a) & (b) Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
58.t:
58. Whoever intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that
he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable
with death or imprisonment for life, voluntarily conceals by any act
or omission, or by the use of encryption or any other information
hiding tool, the existence of a design to commit such offence or
makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting
such design shall,––
(a) if that offence be committed, be punished with imprisonment
of either description for a term which may extend to seven years;
or
(b) if the offence be not committed, with imprisonment of either
description, for a term which may extend to three years, and shall
also be liable to fine.

67.h: Sexual intercourse by husband upon his wife during separation.
67.t:
67. Whoever has sexual intercourse with his own wife, who is living
separately, whether under a decree of separation or otherwise,
without her consent, shall be punished with imprisonment of
either description for a term which shall not be less than two years
but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to
fine.
Explanation.—In this section, “sexual intercourse” shall mean any
of the acts mentioned in clauses (a) to (d) of section 63.

74.h: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty.
74.t:
74. Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman,
intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby
outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of
either description for a term which shall not be less than one year
but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
75 (2)    Sexual harassment
(1) A man committing any of the following acts:—
(i) physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit
sexual overtures; or
(ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or
(iii) showing pornography against the will of a woman; or
(iv) making sexually coloured remarks,shall be guilty of the offence
of sexual harassment.
(2) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause (i) or
clause (ii) or clause (iii)of sub-section (1) shall be punished with
rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years,
or with fine, or with both.
(3) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause (iv) of
sub-section (1)shall be punished with imprisonment of either
description for a term which may extend to one year,or with fine,
or with both.

76.h: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to disrobe.
76.t:
76. Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman or abets
such act with the intention of disrobing or compelling her to be
naked, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description
for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may
extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

77.t:
77. Whoever watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging
in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the
expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by
any other person at the behest of the perpetrator or disseminates
such image shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment
of either description for a term which shall not be less than one
year, but which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable
to fine, and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction,
with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not
be less than three years, but which may extend to seven years, and
shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation 1.—For the purposes of this section, “private act”
includes an act of watching carried out in a place which, in the
circumstances, would reasonably be expected to provide privacy
and where the victim’s genitals, posterior or breasts are exposed or
covered only in underwear; or the victim is using a lavatory; or the
victim is doing a sexual act that is not of a kind ordinarily done in
public.
Explanation 2.—Where the victim consents to the capture of the
images or any act, but not to their dissemination to third persons
and where such image or act is disseminated, such dissemination
shall be considered an offence under this section.

78.t:
78. (1) Any man who—
(i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such
woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear
indication of disinterest by such woman; or
(ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, e-mail or any
other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of
stalking:
Provided that such conduct shall not amount to stalking if the man
who pursued it proves that—
(i) it was pursued for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime
and the man accused of stalking had been entrusted with the
responsibility of prevention and detection of crime by the State; or
(ii) it was pursued under any law or to comply with any condition
or requirement imposed by any person under any law; or
(iii) in the particular circumstances such conduct was reasonable
and justified.
(2) Whoever commits the offence of stalking shall be punished
on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a
term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to
fine; and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with
imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend
to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

79.h: Word, gesture or act intended to insult modesty of a woman
79.t:
79. Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters
any words, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object
in any form, intending that such word or sound shall be heard,
or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman, or
intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with
simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years,
and also with fine.
82(1)       82. (1) Whoever, having a husband or wife living, marries in any
case in which such marriage is void by reason of its taking place
during the life of such husband or wife, shall be punished with
imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend
to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Exception.—This sub-section does not extend to any person

void by a Court of competent jurisdiction, nor to any person who

as being alive within that time provided the person contracting
such subsequent marriage shall, before such marriage takes place,
inform the person with whom such marriage is contracted of the
real state of facts so far as the same are within his or her knowledge.

83.h: Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage.
83.t:
83. Whoever, dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention, goes
through the ceremony of being married, knowing that he is not
thereby lawfully married, shall be punished with imprisonment of
either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and
shall also be liable to fine.
85        Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to
cruelty
Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a
woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with
imprisonment for a term which may extend tothree years and shall
also be liable to fine.

88.t:
88. Whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry,
shall, if such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose
of saving the life of the woman, be punished with imprisonment of
either description for a term which may extend to three years, or
with fine, or with both; and, if the woman be quick with child, shall
be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term
which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.—A woman who causes herself to miscarry, is within
the meaning of this section.

93.h: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years of age, by parent or person having care of it.
93.t:
93. Whoever being the father or mother of a child under the age of
twelve years, or having the care of such child, shall expose or leave
such child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning
such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either
description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with
fine, or with both.
Explanation.—This section is not intended to prevent the trial of
the offender for murder or culpable homicide, as the case may be,
if the child die in consequence of the exposure.

95.h: Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence.
95.t:
95. Whoever hires, employs or engages any child to commit an
offence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description
which shall not be less than three years but which may extend
to ten years, and with fine; and if the offence be committed shall
also be punished with the punishment provided for that offence
as if the offence has been committed by such person himself.
Explanation.—Hiring, employing, engaging or using a child for
sexual exploitation or pornography is covered within the meaning
of this section.

95.h: Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence
95.t:
95. Whoever hires, employs or engages any child to commit an
offence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description
which shall not be less than three years but which may extend

97.h: Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years of age with intent to steal from its person
97.t:
97. Whoever kidnaps or abducts any child under the age of ten
years with the intention of taking dishonestly any movable
property from the person of such child, shall be punished with
imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend
to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

106.t:
106. (1) Whoever causes death of any person by doing any rash
or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be
punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which
may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if such
act is done by a registered medical practitioner while performing
medical procedure, he shall be punished with imprisonment of
either description for a term which may extend to two years, and
shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.— For the purposes of this sub-section, “registered
medical practitioner” means a medical practitioner who possesses
any medical qualification recognised under the National Medical
Commission Act, 2019 and whose name has been entered in the
National Medical Register or a State Medical Register under that
